title: If You Have Multiple Interests, Please Take Advantage of the Next 10 Years

sentences.en: I believe that there will be three types of people in the future, and I think that the divide is growing bigger between them every single day.
sentences.zh: 我相信未来会有三种人，而且这三种人之间的鸿沟每一天都在越拉越大。

sentences.en: And if you want to win or succeed in the next ten years, very uncertain, ten years with where AI and everything else is going.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在未来十年里赢、想成功，在AI和一切都充满不确定性的这十年里——

sentences.en: Then it is critical that you avoid becoming the first or second type of person.
sentences.zh: 那么最关键的就是，别让自己变成第一种或第二种人。

sentences.en: And the first type of person are the purists.
sentences.zh: 第一种人，是纯粹主义者。

sentences.en: They are the ones who think that they stayed clean.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己保持了纯洁。

sentences.en: You know, in Harry Potter there's the pure bloods and the mud bloods.
sentences.zh: 就像《哈利·波特》里有纯血统和泥巴种。

sentences.en: The purists in the context of today's world are the ones who reject AI.
sentences.zh: 在今天这个世界里，纯粹主义者就是那些拒绝AI的人。

sentences.en: They want nothing to do with it, and they retreat to simplicity or nature or screen free living when they're usually the ones who are on their screens the most.
sentences.zh: 他们不想跟AI扯上任何关系，退回到简单、自然、无屏幕的生活，但讽刺的是，他们往往是屏幕用得最凶的那群人。

sentences.en: And they don't realize that simply by using the internet or using social media, they are contributing to the spread of AI.
sentences.zh: 他们没有意识到，光是使用互联网或社交媒体，就已经在助长AI的扩散了。

sentences.en: And when you look at a purist, you can't tell if they're actually being serious or if they're doing it just because it's the cool thing to do, and they're doing it just because everyone else is doing it.
sentences.zh: 而且你看一个纯粹主义者的时候，根本分不清他们是认真的，还是只是因为这么做看起来很酷、只是因为别人都在这么做。

sentences.en: The second type of people are the automatons or the cyborgs.
sentences.zh: 第二种人，是自动机器，或者说半机械人。

sentences.en: They're the ones that outsource every decision.
sentences.zh: 他们把每一个决定都外包出去。

sentences.en: They fully adopt tech without any critical thought, and it ends up ruining their brain.
sentences.zh: 他们毫无批判地全盘接受技术，最终毁掉了自己的大脑。

sentences.en: And that's only on the tech side of things, right?
sentences.zh: 这还只是技术层面，对吧？

sentences.en: There's the health side of things where there's the new peptides and everything else, and these are the very risk forward people.
sentences.zh: 健康层面也一样，各种新的肽类物质层出不穷，这群人是极度拥抱风险的人。

sentences.en: They're willing to just inject anything into their body, and they are all about the future.
sentences.zh: 他们愿意往身体里注射任何东西，他们完全为未来而活。

sentences.en: They're allergic to friction and addicted to optimization.
sentences.zh: 他们对摩擦过敏，对优化上瘾。

sentences.en: They just optimize and automate every single part of their life.
sentences.zh: 他们优化和自动化生活中的每一个部分。

sentences.en: This is the next evolution of the notion template and second brain people, which I have nothing against.
sentences.zh: 这是Notion模板和第二大脑人群的下一个进化阶段——我对这些人本身没什么意见。

sentences.en: Honestly, the second type of person is the one that I lean more towards than the first type of person, because the purists or the first type of person are just so annoying, even if they're right.
sentences.zh: 说实话，比起第一种人，我更偏向第二种人，因为纯粹主义者、也就是第一种人实在太烦人了，就算他们是对的。

sentences.en: Like I don't even want to be associated with them, but the automatons or the cyborgs don't know where AI ends and life begins.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不想跟他们扯上关系。但自动机器或半机械人，他们分不清AI在哪里结束、生活在哪里开始。

sentences.en: And just like with politics or religion or any other kind of ideology, most people think that they have to pick a side because it's just how they're wired.
sentences.zh: 就像政治、宗教或任何其他意识形态一样，大多数人觉得自己必须选边站，因为他们天生就是这样被设定的。

sentences.en: You want to be accepted by a tribe so that you don't cast out, and so you can survive, and so you don't die.
sentences.zh: 你想被某个部落接纳，这样你就不会被驱逐，这样你就能活下来，这样你就不会死。

sentences.en: But personally, I like to be different from most people.
sentences.zh: 但就我个人而言，我喜欢跟大多数人不一样。

sentences.en: Maybe it's a character flaw, maybe it sounds cringe or corny, but I find joy in it.
sentences.zh: 也许这是个性格缺陷，也许听起来很尬、很土，但我从中找到了乐趣。

sentences.en: I think it's a creative challenge to live a life that very few people live, and I found that growth, and therefore meaning and fulfillment does not come from following the herd.
sentences.zh: 我觉得过一种极少数人过的生活，是一个创造性的挑战，而且我发现，成长——以及由此而来的意义和满足感——并不来自于随大流。

sentences.en: So I'm convinced that both sides are wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我确信，两边都错了。

sentences.en: You don't need to fully reject AI and you don't need to fully adopt it.
sentences.zh: 你不需要完全拒绝AI，也不需要全盘接受它。

sentences.en: Crazy to think that way, I know, and if we look at the four quadrants of reality, there's mind, body, spirit and vocation or career or just like the external system society, we have the upper left quadrant, which is the personal mental world or the interior individual.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这么想很疯狂。如果我们看看现实的四个象限——心智、身体、精神，以及职业或事业，或者说外部系统、社会——我们有左上象限，也就是个人的心智世界，或者说内在个体。

sentences.en: So your thoughts, emotions, beliefs and internal world, it's how you interpret the world.
sentences.zh: 也就是你的思想、情绪、信念和内在世界，是你如何解读世界。

sentences.en: And then you have the upper right quadrant, which is the personal physical world or the individual exterior.
sentences.zh: 然后是右上象限，个人的物理世界，或者说个体外在。

sentences.en: And this is your behavior and appearance or it's how the world interprets you.
sentences.zh: 这是你的行为和外表，或者说世界如何解读你。

sentences.en: It's your habits and actions.
sentences.zh: 是你的习惯和行动。

sentences.en: And then you have the bottom left quadrant, which is the collective mental world or the collective interior.
sentences.zh: 然后是左下象限，集体的心智世界，或者说集体内在。

sentences.en: And this is your relationship to your environment, culture, family, friends and reality. It's meaning and connection.
sentences.zh: 这是你与环境、文化、家庭、朋友和现实的关系，关乎意义与连接。

sentences.en: It's your relationship with the external world.
sentences.zh: 是你与外部世界的关系。

sentences.en: And then you have the bottom right quadrant, which is the collective physical world or the collective exterior.
sentences.zh: 然后是右下象限，集体物理世界，或者说集体外部。

sentences.en: So your relationship to society, your education, your career, the economy, how you contribute to the world.
sentences.zh: 也就是你与社会、教育、职业、经济的关系，以及你如何为世界做出贡献。

sentences.en: And of course, this is adapted from Ken Wilbur's Integral theory, which I encourage everyone to explore.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个框架源自 Ken Wilbur 的整合理论，我强烈建议每个人都去了解一下。

sentences.en: Now, the problem is that the purists reject the external world, and this is nothing new.
sentences.zh: 问题是，纯粹主义者排斥外部世界，这并不新鲜。

sentences.en: The hippies and the people who identify too heavily with their spirituality tend to do this as well.
sentences.zh: 嬉皮士和那些过度认同自己灵性身份的人，往往也这么做。

sentences.en: And then the automatons, or the cyborgs, or the people who fully adopt tech.
sentences.zh: 而自动人、半机械人，或者那些完全拥抱科技的人，

sentences.en: They tend to reject the internal world, so they focus fully on money, power, technology, progress, etc. but that is obviously destructive to your potential because you are rejecting an entire portion of reality.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于排斥内部世界，只关注金钱、权力、技术、进步等等，但这显然会摧毁你的潜能，因为你在拒绝整个现实的一部分。

sentences.en: I want you to think of this like a skill tree in a video game.
sentences.zh: 我想让你把它想象成电子游戏里的技能树。

sentences.en: So when you play a video game, you have these abilities, and when you gain experience, you get points that you can put into each ability.
sentences.zh: 你玩游戏的时候，有各种能力，获得经验后，你会得到点数，可以分配到每个能力上。

sentences.en: So like strength, intellect, stamina, etc. so as you level up, you can put a bunch into strength and you get really strong.
sentences.zh: 比如力量、智力、耐力等等。随着你升级，你可以把大量点数投入力量，变得非常强壮。

sentences.en: But the thing is, is that these interconnect, if you only put points in strength, you're obviously going to be at a disadvantage in different parts of the game, and you're going to lose more battles than you win.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这些能力是相互关联的。如果你只加力量，在游戏的不同阶段你显然会处于劣势，输掉的战斗会比赢的多。

sentences.en: And typically in video games, you can only put so many points in strength before it forces you to start putting them in intellect because they interconnect.
sentences.zh: 而且通常游戏里，力量加到一定程度，就会强制你开始加智力，因为它们相互关联。

sentences.en: So the actual example in the real world that applies to your life is that you can try to max out your money or your finances or just go all in on business.
sentences.zh: 对应到你现实生活中的实际例子就是，你可以拼命把金钱或财务拉满，或者全力投入商业。

sentences.en: But if you haven't improved your mind, body or spirit at all, then obviously you're only going to be able to go so far and make so much money or take your business. So far.
sentences.zh: 但如果你完全没有提升你的心智、身体或精神，那你显然只能走到这么远，赚到这么多钱，或者把生意做到这么大。

sentences.en: There comes a time where you have to improve your mind, or maybe you get to the point of being so burnt out and stressed out that you have to lean into spirituality because more money is not going to solve that problem.
sentences.zh: 总有一个时刻，你必须提升你的心智。或者你可能被逼到极度倦怠和压力爆棚的地步，不得不转向灵性，因为更多的钱解决不了那个问题。

sentences.en: Another example is that it doesn't matter how spiritual or enlightened you are, if your body is frail and you're unhealthy, and if you don't have any money to your name, which is the lifeblood of society, you're just going to suffer unnecessarily and more.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是，不管你有多灵性、多开悟，如果你的身体虚弱、不健康，如果你名下没有任何钱——钱是社会的命脉——你只会承受更多不必要的痛苦。

sentences.en: Spirituality is not going to solve that problem because it's not in the same domain of reality.
sentences.zh: 灵性解决不了那个问题，因为它不在同一个现实领域里。

sentences.en: And even further, the solution to your problems that lies in the other domains like money you consider evil or you reject it so you have no choice but to just play the victim.
sentences.zh: 更进一步说，你的问题明明在其他领域有解，比如金钱，但你却认为它是邪恶的，或者排斥它，于是你除了扮演受害者之外别无选择。

sentences.en: So obviously, being a purist isn't the right move.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，做纯粹主义者不是正确的路。

sentences.en: Being an automaton or cyborg isn't the right move.
sentences.zh: 做自动人或半机械人也不是正确的路。

sentences.en: And I think that there is a third option, and that is to become multi-dimensional, to become a new Renaissance man, a digital Renaissance man.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有第三种选择，那就是成为多维的人，成为一个新的文艺复兴人，一个数字文艺复兴人。

sentences.en: So here is how you win in the next ten years.
sentences.zh: 接下来，是你如何在未来十年取胜。

sentences.en: We're in the middle of the Second Renaissance where proof of work replaces the resume, an audience replaces the employer, and taste replaces credentials.
sentences.zh: 我们正处在第二次文艺复兴的中期，工作证明取代简历，受众取代雇主，品味取代证书。

sentences.en: And I believe that the greatest tragedy of our times is that we were fooled into believing that the mechanical life is the only path to success.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们这个时代最大的悲剧，就是我们被骗去相信机械式的生活是通往成功的唯一道路。

sentences.en: You were told to pick a lane.
sentences.zh: 你被告知要选一条路。

sentences.en: You were convinced that having multiple interests was a character flaw.
sentences.zh: 你被说服，拥有多种兴趣是一种性格缺陷。

sentences.en: Become a designer.
sentences.zh: 成为一个设计师。

sentences.en: Become a writer, become an engineer, a marketer, a salesman, or just get whatever high paying job you can because that's how you become respected, quote unquote, and live a good life, quote unquote.
sentences.zh: 成为一个作家，成为一个工程师，一个营销人，一个销售，或者随便找个你能找到的高薪工作，因为这样你才能变得“受人尊敬”，过上“好生活”。

sentences.en: And honestly, that felt pretty reasonable 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 老实说，20年前这听起来还挺合理。

sentences.en: But now you just feel replaceable because that was never how humans were meant to live.
sentences.zh: 但现在你只会觉得自己可以被替代，因为这从来不是人类该有的活法。

sentences.en: And fun fact the modern version of a job, what we call a job today, is only about 250 years old.
sentences.zh: 一个有趣的事实是，现代版本的工作，我们今天所说的“工作”，只有大约250年的历史。

sentences.en: It is so normal for us to just get a job nowadays, or a job is how you survive.
sentences.zh: 如今，找份工作对我们来说太正常了，或者说，工作成了你生存的方式。

sentences.en: When that wasn't the case for hundreds upon hundreds of years, modern life is just a small little sliver and we think we have it all figured out, but we don't. Before the modern version of the job, the ideal was a free person who knew how to do many things throughout their life and pursued their own vision, compared to a slave who was expected to do one specialized task in repetitive tasks, aka the modern version of a job,
sentences.zh: 但在此之前的几百年里，情况根本不是这样。现代生活只是历史长河中的一小段，我们却以为自己什么都搞明白了，其实并没有。在现代意义上的"工作"出现之前，理想的人是自由人——他们一生中懂得做很多事情，追求自己的愿景；与之相对的奴隶，则被要求重复性地完成一项专门任务，也就是现代工作的原型。

sentences.en: the artisan, the farmer, and the pirate are all examples of those who knew how to run an entire operation, not just one specialized piece of it.
sentences.zh: 工匠、农民、海盗，都是懂得如何运营整个事业的人，而不是只会其中某一个环节。

sentences.en: They were both the thinker and the maker, the artist and the scientist.
sentences.zh: 他们既是思考者，也是创造者；既是艺术家，也是科学家。

sentences.en: They understood that in order to live a good life, they could not be limited to one area of study.
sentences.zh: 他们明白，要过好这一生，就不能把自己局限在单一的学习领域。

sentences.en: Leonardo da Vinci walked into Verrocchio workshop to learn painting and left knowing anatomy, engineering, optics and bronze casting.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇走进韦罗基奥的工作室学绘画，离开时却掌握了解剖学、工程学、光学和青铜铸造。

sentences.en: Nobody told him these were separate things that were supposed to be learned as their own credential or degree, and that combination of things is what made him one of the greats in the Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 没人告诉他这些东西是彼此独立的、需要分别拿个文凭或学位才能学，而正是这种跨领域的组合，让他成为文艺复兴时期的巨匠之一。

sentences.en: The previous Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 上一次文艺复兴。

sentences.en: Nobody gave a shit about your niche.
sentences.zh: 没人在乎你的细分定位。

sentences.en: They gave a shit about what you were capable of.
sentences.zh: 他们在乎的是你有什么能力。

sentences.en: And during industrialization, the factory model wasn't meant to destroy education, critical thinking, individual agency and taste.
sentences.zh: 工业化时期，工厂模式的本意并不是摧毁教育、批判性思维、个人能动性和品味。

sentences.en: But that's exactly what it did.
sentences.zh: 但它恰恰造成了这个结果。

sentences.en: It steered us away from the Renaissance ideal.
sentences.zh: 它把我们带离了文艺复兴的理想。

sentences.en: Education became training instead of discovery.
sentences.zh: 教育变成了训练，而不是探索。

sentences.en: Employment and repetitive tasks kept us dumb to the entire entrepreneurial process, so we didn't develop the experience or agency to do our own thing.
sentences.zh: 就业和重复性任务让我们对整个创业过程一无所知，所以我们没能培养出做自己事情的阅历和能动性。

sentences.en: And the unfortunate reality is that this is normal to us.
sentences.zh: 而不幸的现实是，这对我们来说已经成了常态。

sentences.en: The linear career is normal to us instead of the exponential career, and the masses just don't question it.
sentences.zh: 线性职业成了常态，指数型职业反而被忽视，而大众对此毫不质疑。

sentences.en: And now that AI is on our doorstep, only those with an open mind and those who don't identify with a team that fully rejects the next phase of evolution will take advantage of this shift.
sentences.zh: 如今 AI 已经来到我们门前，只有那些心态开放的人、那些不把自己归属于全盘拒绝下一阶段进化的阵营的人，才能抓住这次转变的机会。

sentences.en: One person can now do what a 10 to 50% team used to do, depending on the task, one person now has any and all known information at their fingertips, and I want to highlight the word known.
sentences.zh: 一个人现在可以完成过去需要 10 到 50 人团队才能做的事，具体取决于任务类型。一个人现在可以随时调取所有已知信息，我想强调"已知"这个词。

sentences.en: That's what AI is good at.
sentences.zh: 这就是 AI 擅长的东西。

sentences.en: Known information, not unknown or novel information that comes from experience and diving into the unknown and pursuing an unknown path.
sentences.zh: 已知信息，而不是未知的、新颖的信息——那些来自亲身经历、来自踏入未知领域、来自走一条未知之路的信息。

sentences.en: That's what your job is, and that shines a light on how you can incorporate AI.
sentences.zh: 那才是你的任务，而这也指明了你可以如何运用 AI。

sentences.en: And along with access to all known information, one person has access to social media.
sentences.zh: 除了能获取所有已知信息，一个人还拥有社交媒体。

sentences.en: One person media companies, aka creators, are popping up left and right because it's free distribution for their work if they understand media attention, human psychology, etc..
sentences.zh: 一人媒体公司，也就是创作者，正在遍地开花，因为只要他们理解媒体注意力、人性心理等等，这就是他们作品的免费分发渠道。

sentences.en: So if you are a true new Renaissance man, or digital Renaissance man or person or girl, whatever it is, it doesn't have to be a man.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是一个真正的新文艺复兴人，或者数字文艺复兴人，不管男女，叫什么都可以，不一定非得是"人"。

sentences.en: You can be a new Renaissance toaster oven for all I care.
sentences.zh: 你想叫新文艺复兴烤面包机我也不在乎。

sentences.en: If you are one of these people, this is the greatest time to be alive.
sentences.zh: 如果你是这类人，现在就是有史以来最好的时代。

sentences.en: No exaggeration, no hype.
sentences.zh: 毫不夸张，不是炒作。

sentences.en: It's obvious, and many people will try to convince you that the world is doomed.
sentences.zh: 这显而易见，但很多人会试图说服你世界要完蛋了。

sentences.en: AI can now handle the machine like repetitive tasks that for the past two centuries, used to be our entire way of life.
sentences.zh: AI 现在可以处理那些机器般的重复性任务，而在过去两个世纪里，这些任务曾是我们生活的全部。

sentences.en: People are so worried that AI will ruin our thinking and make us more like machines, when they've already been living like machines for the whole of their lives.
sentences.zh: 人们非常担心 AI 会毁掉我们的思考能力、让我们变得更像机器，可他们自己一辈子本来就已经活得像机器了。

sentences.en: Seriously, think about that. I hate that argument.
sentences.zh: 说真的，好好想想。我烦透那个论调了。

sentences.en: AI is going to ruin your thinking.
sentences.zh: AI 会毁掉你的思考。

sentences.en: A is going to make you more robotic and strip away your humanity.
sentences.zh: AI 会让你变得更机械，剥夺你的人性。

sentences.en: What have the past 200 years been?
sentences.zh: 那过去 200 年又算什么？

sentences.en: It's been exactly that, and you've been living it, and you're just regurgitating the program that was put into your mind.
sentences.zh: 过去 200 年就是这副模样，你一直活在其中，你只是在反刍别人塞进你脑子里的程序。

sentences.en: That is the anti AI ideology.
sentences.zh: 这就是反 AI 的意识形态。

sentences.en: If that is not a machine and a lack of critical thinking, I don't know what is.
sentences.zh: 如果这都不算机器、不算缺乏批判性思维，那我真不知道什么才算。

sentences.en: So to those who join this second renaissance, your job is to choose your craft, leverage AI so that you can manage the entire operation aka your life's work, and focus on taste, direction, and judgment.
sentences.zh: 所以对那些加入这第二次文艺复兴的人来说，你的任务是选定你的手艺，用 AI 做杠杆来管理整个运作——也就是你一生的事业——然后把精力放在品味、方向和判断上。

sentences.en: Because the output of AI does not have perspective, AI is simply that artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 因为 AI 的输出没有视角，AI 就是人工智"能"而已。

sentences.en: It's like a bag of water that you must mold.
sentences.zh: 它就像一袋水，你得自己去塑形。

sentences.en: So the point is that you must become a multi-dimensional, irreplaceable walking contradiction, because the most interesting people are just that.
sentences.zh: 所以重点是，你必须成为一个多维度的、不可替代的行走矛盾体，因为最有趣的人恰恰就是这种人。

sentences.en: They're walking contradictions, jacked intellectuals, casual billionaires, spiritual warriors.
sentences.zh: 他们是行走的矛盾体：肌肉发达的知识分子、随意的亿万富翁、灵性的战士。

sentences.en: Life is better when you can't be shoved into a box that others can easily make sense of in the future, the most interesting and valuable people will be those who live between two extremes pure creativity and pure productivity.
sentences.zh: 当别人没法把你塞进一个容易理解的盒子里时，人生会好得多。未来，最有趣、最有价值的人会是那些活在两个极端之间的人：纯粹的创造力和纯粹的生产力。

sentences.en: They seamlessly balance the analog lifestyle of no screens, reading books, maintaining their humanity, doing the things that lead to novel ideas and novel experiences.
sentences.zh: 他们无缝地平衡着两种生活：一种是模拟生活方式，没有屏幕、读书、保持自己的人性、做那些能带来新颖想法和新颖体验的事。

sentences.en: No urgency, just pure life enjoyment and the AI native productive lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 没有紧迫感，只是纯粹地享受生活；另一种是 AI 原生的生产力生活方式。

sentences.en: Or leveraging technology to do what used to be impossible.
sentences.zh: 或者说，用技术去做过去不可能做到的事。

sentences.en: So it's between the two extremes of reading a book in a park, carefree, and being locked in hustle culture to your computer because both are very enjoyable ways to live.
sentences.zh: 所以就是在两个极端之间：在公园里无忧无虑地读一本书，和把自己锁在电脑前进入奋斗文化——因为这两种生活方式都非常令人享受。

sentences.en: It's narrow, focused flow state getting work done at your computer, which many people have experienced and it feels really good.
sentences.zh: 一种是在电脑前进入狭窄、专注的心流状态把工作做完，很多人都体验过，感觉真的很好。

sentences.en: And then on the other end, it's a very open state of focus where you're more connected with reality.
sentences.zh: 而另一端，是一种非常开放、你与现实连接更深的专注状态。

sentences.en: That's where the spirituality comes into play.
sentences.zh: 灵性就是从这里进来的。

sentences.en: And by doing that, you experience the full range of consciousness and focus along with that, meaning and fulfillment are not found in a flat, balanced lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，你会体验到意识和专注的完整光谱。而意义和满足感，不是在一个平坦、平衡的生活方式里找到的。

sentences.en: They are found in contrast, because if you were happy all the time, you wouldn't consider it happiness.
sentences.zh: 它们是在对比中找到的。因为你如果一直快乐，你就不会觉得那是快乐。

sentences.en: You would consider it normal and honestly, it would be a bit boring.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得那是正常，而且说实话，会有点无聊。

sentences.en: You would need greater and greater euphoria to feel what you think happiness is.
sentences.zh: 你会需要越来越大的快感才能感受到你以为的快乐是什么。

sentences.en: Hence why people can't get off their phones today because a normal happy life is too boring for them.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么今天人们放不下手机，因为一个正常、快乐的生活对他们来说太无聊了。

sentences.en: But when you fail and you struggle and you suffer for something that you care about, you learn what true happiness is on the other side.
sentences.zh: 但当你为你真正在乎的事情失败、挣扎、受苦时，你才会在另一端学会什么是真正的快乐。

sentences.en: So those who win will lean into that contrast.
sentences.zh: 所以那些会赢的人，会主动拥抱这种对比。

sentences.en: They work and they rest deeply.
sentences.zh: 他们深度工作，也深度休息。

sentences.en: Their entire life is play because they love what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们的整个人生就是玩，因为他们热爱自己正在做的事。

sentences.en: They have intense bursts of focus on their craft, followed by complete and deep rest, just like the world's most creative people do.
sentences.zh: 他们在自己的手艺上有高强度的专注爆发，然后是完全的、深度的休息，就像世界上最有创造力的人所做的那样。

sentences.en: And you can see that in this graphic.
sentences.zh: 你可以在这张图里看到。

sentences.en: The daily routines of famous creative people, as one example that I love, Charles Darwin wrote 19 books in his lifetime, which is just absurd in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 著名创意人士的日常作息，举一个我很喜欢的例子：查尔斯·达尔文一生写了 19 本书，这本身就已经很离谱了。

sentences.en: But his morning routine would surprise people for that level of output.
sentences.zh: 但他的晨间作息，以那样的产出水平来看，会让人大吃一惊。

sentences.en: At 7 a.m., he went on a short walk and then had breakfast from 8 to 930.
sentences.zh: 早上 7 点，他去散一小段步，然后 8 点到 9 点半吃早餐。

sentences.en: He had his first work session in his study, and this was his most creative block.
sentences.zh: 9 点半到 10 点半，他在书房进行第一个工作时段，这是他最有创造力的时间段。

sentences.en: From 930 to 1030 he had a break to read letters and spend time with family.
sentences.zh: 10 点半到 12 点，他休息，读信、陪家人。

sentences.en: Then from 1030 to noon he had his second work session, and by this point Darwin considered himself to have done a good day's work.
sentences.zh: 然后 12 点到下午 2 点，是他的第二个工作时段。到这个时候，达尔文就认为自己已经完成了一天中足够好的工作了。

sentences.en: Then afternoon he had a second walk of the day around the sand walk, which is a famous quarter mile gravel path that he built specifically for thinking and reflection.
sentences.zh: 下午他会进行当天的第二次散步，沿着沙径走——那是一条著名的、大约 400 米长的碎石路，他专门为了思考和反思而修建的。

sentences.en: I really want to do that one day.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想有一天也这么做。

sentences.en: Imagine building your own walking path.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，建一条属于自己的散步小径。

sentences.en: I love walks, I go on walks and the time.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢散步，我经常散步，而且一直在坚持。

sentences.en: It is the crux of idea generation and my work, and that is how I balance out the intense focus productivity at my computer with a more open state of creative focus.
sentences.zh: 这是我产生想法和工作的关键，我就是这样平衡电脑前高强度专注产出和更开放的创造性专注状态的。

sentences.en: Then after lunch, Darwin read the newspaper, then rested while his wife read aloud to him. At 4 p.m. he had the third walk of the day, usually around the sand.
sentences.zh: 午饭后，达尔文读报纸，然后休息，妻子给他朗读。下午四点，他开始第三次散步，通常是在沙地上。

sentences.en: Walk again, sometimes with company.
sentences.zh: 又去散步，有时候有人陪着。

sentences.en: So Darwin worked roughly three hours of focus creative work per day across two sessions, and he has contributed vastly to humanity and wrote 19 books.
sentences.zh: 所以达尔文每天大概只做三个小时的专注创造性工作，分两个时段，但他对人类贡献巨大，写了19本书。

sentences.en: That's just absurd.
sentences.zh: 这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: So imagine what you can do if you were fully locked in on this path.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，如果你完全锁定在这条路上，你能做成什么。

sentences.en: I believe that there will be ten times more Darwin's and da Vinci's of today's world, simply because of the resources available to you.
sentences.zh: 我相信，当今世界会出现十倍于达尔文和达芬奇的人，仅仅因为你手头可用的资源。

sentences.en: There will be ten times more.
sentences.zh: 会多出十倍。

sentences.en: Plato's. Aristotle, Socrates.
sentences.zh: 柏拉图、亚里士多德、苏格拉底。

sentences.en: But of course, we won't realize that until later into the future, because unfortunately, we don't really care about people's work that much until they're dead, because the death brings a different kind of meaning to the work.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们要到未来才会意识到这一点，因为不幸的是，我们通常不太在意一个人的作品，直到他死了，因为死亡给作品赋予了一种不同的意义。

sentences.en: And we can already see this playing out.
sentences.zh: 而我们已经能看到这正在发生。

sentences.en: There are plenty of brilliant people online sharing their knowledge. It's crazy.
sentences.zh: 网上有大量聪明人在分享他们的知识。这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I have learned more from YouTube than I ever did in school, and I will stand by that.
sentences.zh: 我从YouTube学到的东西比在学校学到的多得多，我坚持这个说法。

sentences.en: So I believe that the people of the future who are going to thrive will have some variation of this kind of routine, but with the output of 10 to 20 people, allowing you to do so much more and you'll be able to single handedly build your life's work.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信，未来那些会蓬勃发展的人，都会有某种类似这样的日常，但产出相当于10到20个人，让你能做多得多的事情，你能够单枪匹马地构建你一生的事业。

sentences.en: Or you can have an incredibly small team and just do so much.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以有一个极小的团队，然后做成这么多事。

sentences.en: So, in other words, these people will have a one human business, one human with technology agents, AI at their side, and we will break down how to build this one human business in another video and a quote from navel that kind of points at this is there are almost 7 billion people on this planet.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这些人会拥有一个一人企业，一个人加上技术代理、AI在身旁，我们会在另一个视频里拆解如何构建这个一人企业。Naval有一句话指向了这一点：这个星球上有将近70亿人。

sentences.en: Someday I hope there will be almost 7 billion companies.
sentences.zh: 我希望有一天，会有将近70亿家公司。

sentences.en: We are getting closer and closer to that reality.
sentences.zh: 我们离那个现实越来越近了。

sentences.en: I don't know whether all jobs are going to go away, but I really like that ideal.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是不是所有工作都会消失，但我真的很喜欢那个理想。

sentences.en: I believe that humans are entrepreneurial creatures, not in the business sense, but in the sense that engaging with reality, the process of trial and error is the most meaningful and creative way to live.
sentences.zh: 我相信人类是天生的创业型生物，不是商业意义上的，而是说，与现实互动、试错的过程，是最有意义、最有创造力的生活方式。

sentences.en: Not to be locked in a cubicle doing repetitive tasks all day that is soul sucking.
sentences.zh: 而不是被锁在小隔间里整天做重复性任务，那是在吸走你的灵魂。

sentences.en: We all know that now, before factories and industrialization, you worked until the task was done.
sentences.zh: 我们现在都知道了，在工厂和工业化之前，你是干到活干完为止。

sentences.en: Not until your eight hour shift was over.
sentences.zh: 不是干到你八小时的班结束为止。

sentences.en: You worked according to the rhythm of seasons, sunlight and energy.
sentences.zh: 你按照季节、阳光和精力的节奏来工作。

sentences.en: And more importantly, you didn't learn how to become valuable through a standardized curriculum and meaningless memorization tests.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，你不是通过标准化课程和无意义的记忆考试来学习如何变得有价值。

sentences.en: That's what public schools are.
sentences.zh: 公立学校就是这样的。

sentences.en: Instead, you learned by doing.
sentences.zh: 相反，你是通过做来学。

sentences.en: You learned in the workshop, from apprentice to journeyman to master, imitating someone who knew what they were doing until your own taste and judgment were formed.
sentences.zh: 你在作坊里学习，从学徒到熟练工再到大师，模仿一个知道自己在做什么的人，直到你自己的品味和判断力形成。

sentences.en: So the question now is just that how do you become this new or digital renaissance man?
sentences.zh: 所以现在的问题就是：你如何成为这个新的、或者说数字时代的文艺复兴人？

sentences.en: You do it all.
sentences.zh: 你全都做。

sentences.en: You become a writer, a designer, a marketer, a filmmaker, a bodybuilder or runner or whatever your curiosity desires.
sentences.zh: 你成为一个写作者、设计师、营销者、电影制作人、健身者或跑者，或者任何你好奇心渴望的东西。

sentences.en: But you channel your focus and attention into one vessel, one craft, one thing that you choose to become known for, and your multifaceted development will only contribute to your ability to get ahead of everyone else.
sentences.zh: 但你把专注力和注意力汇聚到一个载体、一门手艺、一件你选择以此成名的事情上，而你多维度的发展只会帮助你领先于所有人。

sentences.en: Not that you have to get ahead of everyone else, but you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 不是说非得领先所有人，但你懂我的意思。

sentences.en: To get ahead in the sense that you are no longer grouped in with the masses. So here's what you do.
sentences.zh: 领先的意思是，你不再被归入大众那一类。所以你要做的是这些。

sentences.en: The first thing is you choose your craft and become irreplaceable.
sentences.zh: 第一件事，选择你的手艺，让自己变得不可替代。

sentences.en: Most artists, writers and creatives that you see online that are revolting against AI do so because they have identified with the skill or the tool or their specific way of working.
sentences.zh: 你在网上看到的大多数反对 AI 的艺术家、写作者和创作者，之所以这么做，是因为他们已经把自己的身份认同绑在了那个技能、那个工具或者他们特定的工作方式上。

sentences.en: And personally, I don't care about the argument of whether or not AI art is real or AI writing is real.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我根本不在乎 AI 艺术是不是真的、AI 写作是不是真的这种争论。

sentences.en: That seems like the greatest distraction of this year, because as you're arguing about that, you weren't creating art.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是今年最大的干扰，因为当你在争论这些的时候，你没有在创作艺术。

sentences.en: You aren't doing the thing that you say you love so much.
sentences.zh: 你没有在做你声称自己无比热爱的那件事。

sentences.en: You aren't focused on your craft.
sentences.zh: 你没有专注于你的手艺。

sentences.en: You aren't getting better.
sentences.zh: 你没有在变得更好。

sentences.en: In fact, you're just trying to bring everyone into this cesspool of hate.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你只是在试图把所有人都拖进这个仇恨的粪坑里。

sentences.en: And most of the time, you're just doing it for the incentive because you know it's going to get a lot of views and likes.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数时候，你这么做只是为了激励，因为你知道这会带来很多观看量和点赞。

sentences.en: And the worst thing is that you're just reinforcing the identity that is not going to serve you in the coming years.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是，你只是在不断强化那个在未来几年对你毫无用处的身份认同。

sentences.en: So you need a craft, but you need to choose your craft wisely.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一门手艺，但你需要明智地选择你的手艺。

sentences.en: Your craft lives at the intersection of what you care about, what you can uniquely do, and what others are willing to pay you for.
sentences.zh: 你的手艺存在于你关心什么、你能独特地做什么、以及别人愿意为什么付钱给你这三者的交汇处。

sentences.en: And in my eyes, there are three layers to building an irreplaceable skill stack.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，构建一个不可替代的技能栈有三个层次。

sentences.en: Layer one is a foundation of human nature or psychology.
sentences.zh: 第一层是人性或心理学的基础。

sentences.en: So marketing, sales, writing, speaking, or just psychology itself, it's understanding the mechanics of human attention and how what people perceive as valuable is highly subjective and changes as the world does.
sentences.zh: 也就是营销、销售、写作、演讲，或者心理学本身，这是理解人类注意力的运作机制，以及人们认为有价值的东西是高度主观的，会随着世界的变化而变化。

sentences.en: Everyone's worried about the dead internet in AI slop, but they don't understand that what people see as valuable changes over time like, oh, if AI just writes all the content, then my content just instantly becomes invaluable when that's not the case, because everyone pumping out the AI content all looks the same, and so people get used to it extremely fast and they no longer see it as valuable.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在担心死寂互联网和 AI 垃圾内容，但他们不明白，人们认为有价值的东西会随着时间改变。比如，哦，如果 AI 写了所有内容，那我的内容岂不是瞬间就变得毫无价值了？事实并非如此，因为每个人都在批量生产的 AI 内容看起来全都一样，所以人们会极快地适应它，不再认为它有价值。

sentences.en: So the humans who actually understand this then use their brain to be creative and do something novel.
sentences.zh: 所以那些真正理解这一点的人类，就会用他们的大脑去发挥创造力，做出新颖的东西。

sentences.en: Marketing and content and product and business is just an extremely iterative process.
sentences.zh: 营销、内容、产品和商业，只是一个极度迭代的过程。

sentences.en: It never stops.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会停。

sentences.en: You're always in this state of trial and error improving.
sentences.zh: 你永远处在这种试错、改进的状态里。

sentences.en: So every single person who wants to succeed on their own must master this domain, this layer one, this is the what others are willing to pay you for.
sentences.zh: 所以每一个想靠自己成功的人，都必须精通这个领域，这第一层，这就是别人愿意为什么付钱给你。

sentences.en: Now, layer two is your domain obsession and unique interests.
sentences.zh: 接下来，第二层是你的领域痴迷和独特的兴趣。

sentences.en: So philosophy, fitness, design, coding, nutrition or anything else none of these are going away. They are simply evolving.
sentences.zh: 比如哲学、健身、设计、编程、营养学或者其他任何东西，这些都不会消失。它们只是在进化。

sentences.en: And of course marketing, sales, writing, psychology, all of those things can also be your obsession.
sentences.zh: 当然，营销、销售、写作、心理学，所有这些也可以成为你的痴迷。

sentences.en: But if they aren't, if those aren't one of your interests, you still have to master that domain.
sentences.zh: 但如果它们不是，如果这些不是你的兴趣之一，你仍然必须精通那个领域。

sentences.en: Now, the combination of these interests is where your uniqueness lies.
sentences.zh: 而这些兴趣的组合，正是你独特性的所在。

sentences.en: So the jacked philosopher is far more valuable than the armchair philosopher, who only grows their mind without direct experience to test their theories, and is just far more interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以一个肌肉发达的哲学家，远比一个纸上谈兵的哲学家有价值得多，后者只增长心智，却没有直接经验去检验他们的理论，而且前者就是有趣得多。

sentences.en: And then you pair that with marketing and sales.
sentences.zh: 然后你再把这跟营销和销售结合起来。

sentences.en: Imagine the Jacques philosopher who actually has a business and a product so they can make money from their jacked philosopher.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，一个肌肉发达的哲学家，实际上拥有一个生意和一个产品，这样他们就能从自己肌肉发达的哲学家身份中赚钱。

sentences.en: They're unstoppable.
sentences.zh: 他们势不可挡。

sentences.en: But you just take someone who's jacked and they look nice, or you just take a philosopher and you think their mind is pretty cool, but nothing else.
sentences.zh: 但如果你只看一个肌肉发达的人，他们看起来不错，或者你只看一个哲学家，你觉得他们的头脑挺酷的，但除此之外，什么都没有。

sentences.en: So this layer is the what you care about and what you uniquely can do layer.
sentences.zh: 所以这一层是你关心什么、你独特能做什么的层面。

sentences.en: And it is the thing that people come to you for over another person.
sentences.zh: 也是人们来找你而不是找别人的原因。

sentences.en: And then layer three is the technical skill.
sentences.zh: 第三层是技术技能。

sentences.en: So like email marketing software or Photoshop or no code, website design or social media management or typing physical code to build a software on the screen.
sentences.zh: 比如邮件营销软件、Photoshop、无代码网站设计、社交媒体管理，或者在屏幕上敲代码做软件。

sentences.en: Now, this used to be the most important because it took time and effort to learn these tools.
sentences.zh: 过去这一层最重要，因为学这些工具需要花时间和精力。

sentences.en: But now AI does it all with ease, so you should not bank your future on mastery of a tool because AI is the ultimate tool.
sentences.zh: 但现在 AI 轻松搞定一切，所以你不该把未来押在精通某个工具上，因为 AI 才是终极工具。

sentences.en: So if your entire identity is a tool like Photoshop, then I hate to say it, but you have a few years left and that may sound like fear mongering, but I think it's a pretty good bet.
sentences.zh: 如果你整个身份认同就是一个工具，比如 Photoshop，那我不想这么说，但你只剩几年了——这听起来像在制造恐慌，但我觉得这个赌注相当靠谱。

sentences.en: And that's just the pattern of every single technological shift.
sentences.zh: 这就是每一次技术变革的规律。

sentences.en: You have to adapt, the mechanical part of the skill gets automated and the human role moves up a layer.
sentences.zh: 你必须适应，技能的机械部分被自动化，人的角色往上移一层。

sentences.en: The scribe became the editor and the hand weaver became the machine operator.
sentences.zh: 抄写员变成了编辑，手工织布工变成了机器操作员。

sentences.en: And we'll discuss more of this in a second.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再多聊这个。

sentences.en: The second part of becoming this new Renaissance man is becoming dangerously self-educated, because schools teach you how to operate within society, which is fine and necessary to some extent, but they do not teach you how to navigate your own path.
sentences.zh: 成为这个新文艺复兴人的第二部分，是变得危险地自我教育，因为学校教你如何在社会里运作，这没问题，某种程度上也必要，但它们不教你如何走自己的路。

sentences.en: Public schools are filtering and conditioning mechanisms more than anything.
sentences.zh: 公立学校更多是筛选和规训机制。

sentences.en: And again, that's fine. It's a necessary evil.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这没问题，是必要的恶。

sentences.en: You have to be conditioned to some point.
sentences.zh: 你必须在某种程度上被规训。

sentences.en: You have to learn how to walk.
sentences.zh: 你得学会走路。

sentences.en: You have to learn how to speak.
sentences.zh: 你得学会说话。

sentences.en: You have to learn how to do basic math.
sentences.zh: 你得学会做基础数学。

sentences.en: You have to learn how to just exist.
sentences.zh: 你得学会怎么存在。

sentences.en: But true education is discovery.
sentences.zh: 但真正的教育是发现。

sentences.en: The education that makes you irreplaceable is discovery.
sentences.zh: 让你不可替代的教育是发现。

sentences.en: It is the process of learning what's necessary to achieve self-generated vision and goals, not the process of hoarding knowledge or memorizing facts to do well on a test that does not map to reality.
sentences.zh: 它是学习实现自我生成的愿景和目标所需之物的过程，不是囤积知识或死记硬背去考一场跟现实脱节的考试。

sentences.en: And even worse, most people stop learning after graduation, graduating high school or college.
sentences.zh: 更糟的是，大多数人毕业后就停止学习了，高中或大学毕业后。

sentences.en: They turn 20 to 25 and repeat the same day for the rest of their life.
sentences.zh: 他们到了 20 到 25 岁，然后余生重复同一天。

sentences.en: They do not pursue a creative challenge that demands unique knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们不去追求需要独特知识的创造性挑战。

sentences.en: They don't have a demand to learn something new.
sentences.zh: 他们没有学新东西的需求。

sentences.en: They don't have a goal or vision so potent that motivates them to wake up in the morning, because honestly, they think that they have to know how to do it before they start, which is backwards.
sentences.zh: 他们没有一个足够强烈的目标或愿景，能激励他们早上起床，因为说实话，他们觉得自己必须先知道怎么做才能开始，这完全是反的。

sentences.en: So how do you actually learn?
sentences.zh: 那你到底怎么学？

sentences.en: How do you become self-educated?
sentences.zh: 你怎么变得自我教育？

sentences.en: Will you follow the apprenticeship model you apprentice under a master or a mentor?
sentences.zh: 你会走学徒模式吗？拜一位大师或导师为师。

sentences.en: And the beautiful thing about today's world is that you can find a mentor or a master simply by picking up a book, or opening your phone and going onto YouTube.
sentences.zh: 当今世界的美妙之处在于，你只需要拿起一本书，或者打开手机上 YouTube，就能找到导师或大师。

sentences.en: And yes, the feed is very crowded and noisy, but that's exactly why you need a vision and goals.
sentences.zh: 是的，信息流非常拥挤嘈杂，但这正是你需要愿景和目标的原因。

sentences.en: Because vision and goals are a filtering mechanism for your mind.
sentences.zh: 因为愿景和目标是心智的筛选机制。

sentences.en: They filter out distractions and allow you to notice signal.
sentences.zh: 它们过滤掉干扰，让你能注意到信号。

sentences.en: If you're working on building a business and you open up YouTube, you're probably not going to be interested in opening some brain style of entertainment Video you're going to be scrolling to find a business video intentionally that helps you get closer to your goals and learn what you need to learn.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在创业，打开 YouTube 的时候，你大概不会想看什么消遣类的娱乐视频，你会刻意去刷那些能帮你靠近目标、学到你需要学的东西的商业视频。

sentences.en: So in other words, you need to live an intentional life.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你必须过一种有意识的生活。

sentences.en: And that's just the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这。

sentences.en: I don't care if you use AI to get information.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎你是不是用 AI 获取信息。

sentences.en: I don't care if you get all your advice from one YouTube guru.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎你是不是所有建议都来自一个 YouTube 大佬。

sentences.en: What I do care about is if you have a vision, have a goal, work toward that goal and apply what you learn to problems that come up along the way.
sentences.zh: 我在乎的是你有没有一个愿景，有没有一个目标，有没有朝着那个目标努力，并且把你学到的东西应用到沿途遇到的问题上。

sentences.en: That is how you test what you learn to verify its validity for your specific situation.
sentences.zh: 只有这样，你才能检验你学到的东西，验证它在你具体情境下是否有效。

sentences.en: Because whether AI hallucinates or not or gives you the wrong information, there are still plenty of profoundly stupid people humans that you probably shouldn't listen to and that give terrible information or completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为不管 AI 会不会胡编乱造、会不会给你错误信息，这世上仍然有一大堆蠢到骨子里的人类，你大概率不该听他们的，他们给的建议烂透了，或者完全错误。

sentences.en: At least the AI doesn't try to lie.
sentences.zh: 至少 AI 不会故意撒谎。

sentences.en: Humans lie all the time, and they will defend their lies to death if they identify with them.
sentences.zh: 人类一直在撒谎，而且如果他们认同那些谎言，他们会至死捍卫。

sentences.en: So either way, both sides are wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以不管哪边，两边都可能出错。

sentences.en: It's up to you to think critically.
sentences.zh: 批判性思考是你自己的事。

sentences.en: You need to question and test and experiment.
sentences.zh: 你需要质疑、测试、实验。

sentences.en: You can only tell if information or advice is worthwhile after you try it.
sentences.zh: 你只有亲自试过之后，才能判断一条信息或建议有没有价值。

sentences.en: You can't watch a YouTube video on how to make $1 million and decide whether it's a scam or not, if you haven't even done anything with it so you don't learn and then do, that's how you get stuck into hell.
sentences.zh: 你看了一个教你怎么赚 100 万美元的 YouTube 视频，如果你什么都没做，你根本没法判断它是不是骗局——所以你不学也不做，这就是你陷入地狱的原因。

sentences.en: You do the thing first or attempt to do the thing, and only then is your mind primed to receive the lesson that allows you to make forward progress.
sentences.zh: 你先去做，或者尝试去做，只有到那个时候，你的大脑才会准备好接收那个能让你向前推进的教训。

sentences.en: So you have your craft.
sentences.zh: 所以你有你的手艺。

sentences.en: You know how to educate yourself. Now what do you do?
sentences.zh: 你知道怎么教育自己。现在你该做什么？

sentences.en: What do you build?
sentences.zh: 你该构建什么？

sentences.en: You build a one human business.
sentences.zh: 你构建一个一人企业。

sentences.en: And I'm talking to people who haven't started anything yet, right?
sentences.zh: 我是在跟那些还没开始做任何事的人说话，对吧？

sentences.en: If you already have a business, you're already deep in this world.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经有了一门生意，你已经深在这个世界里了。

sentences.en: You already know what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 你已经知道我在说什么了。

sentences.en: But you need to start a one human business, and you need to join the new digital economy because creators are replacing institutions.
sentences.zh: 但你需要启动一个一人企业，你需要加入新的数字经济，因为创作者正在取代机构。

sentences.en: And I know that sounds silly, but can you not see it?
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很蠢，但你难道看不见吗？

sentences.en: Creators are the new education system.
sentences.zh: 创作者就是新的教育系统。

sentences.en: Do you not learn most of the things that are actually useful in your life on Substack, YouTube, podcasts, or niche accounts on Twitter?
sentences.zh: 你生活中真正有用的东西，难道不大多是在 Substack、YouTube、播客，或者 Twitter 上的小众账号里学到的吗？

sentences.en: X creators shape, culture and culture shapes behavior.
sentences.zh: X 上的创作者塑造文化，文化塑造行为。

sentences.en: Do you not trust a creator whose thoughts you've spent time with over politicians who obviously have their own self-interest in mind?
sentences.zh: 比起那些明显心怀私利的政客，你难道不更信任一个你花时间读过他思想的创作者吗？

sentences.en: The internet is permissionless leverage.
sentences.zh: 互联网是无须许可的杠杆。

sentences.en: You don't need approval to build an audience or start a business or sell a product.
sentences.zh: 你不需要任何人的批准，就可以构建受众、启动生意、销售产品。

sentences.en: It is the high agency path.
sentences.zh: 这是一条高自主性的路。

sentences.en: And last, AI accelerates the generalist and the polymath, meaning you can actually become a one human business content on social media to attract an audience around your life's work.
sentences.zh: 最后，AI 加速了通才和博学者的崛起，意味着你真的可以成为一个一人企业——用社交媒体内容围绕你一生的事业吸引受众。

sentences.en: Code to build the product funnel, and digital real estate and domain specific knowledge that makes what you do valuable over the next person.
sentences.zh: 用代码构建产品漏斗和数字资产，用领域专长让你做的事情比下一个人更有价值。

sentences.en: And now, when I say creator here, you probably think of an influencer or a personal brand, but that's not exactly what I mean.
sentences.zh: 我说"创作者"的时候，你脑子里可能蹦出的是网红或者个人品牌，但我说的不是这个意思。

sentences.en: I mean someone who creates value.
sentences.zh: 我说的是创造价值的人。

sentences.en: I mean a creator stripped of your connotations with it.
sentences.zh: 我说的是剥掉你所有刻板印象之后的那个"创作者"。

sentences.en: They solve problems, they create solutions, and they help others do the same.
sentences.zh: 他们解决问题，他们创造解决方案，他们还帮别人做同样的事。

sentences.en: And since value exchange is the crux of human relationships, they return the favor, often in the form of money.
sentences.zh: 而价值交换是人际关系的核心，所以对方会回报你，通常是以金钱的形式。

sentences.en: That's how you make money outside of a job.
sentences.zh: 这就是你在打工之外赚钱的方式。

sentences.en: You create something, you create a product or you create a service.
sentences.zh: 你创造点什么，创造一个产品，或者创造一个服务。

sentences.en: I know that sounds very business heavy, but that's what you do.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来商业味很重，但这就是你要做的事。

sentences.en: You create something.
sentences.zh: 你创造点什么。

sentences.en: A product or service is just a way to frame what you've created in a way that is valuable to another person, to the point where they actually pay you for it.
sentences.zh: 产品或服务，只是一种包装你创造的东西的方式，让它对别人有价值，价值大到对方愿意为此付钱。

sentences.en: So you need to create a product or service, and you need to become a creator.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要创造一个产品或服务，你需要成为一个创作者。

sentences.en: And when you think of someone like James Clear, he has a personal brand.
sentences.zh: 你想想 James Clear 这样的人，他有个人品牌。

sentences.en: Yes, but he's really just writing newsletters and books and content to get his life's work in front of more eyes so he can earn an independent income.
sentences.zh: 没错，但他真正做的只是写 newsletter、写书、写内容，把他毕生的作品推到更多人眼前，这样他就能赚到一份独立的收入。

sentences.en: I personally believe that most ambitious individuals will take this route in the future, even if what we know as social media today isn't where you put your work in front of other people.
sentences.zh: 我个人相信，未来大多数有野心的人都会走这条路，哪怕我们今天所知的社交媒体不再是你的作品触达他人的地方。

sentences.en: In the past, it was the newspaper and the radio, and now it's social media.
sentences.zh: 过去是报纸和广播，现在是社交媒体。

sentences.en: But who knows what it will be in the future.
sentences.zh: 但谁知道未来会是什么。

sentences.en: What I know is that starting on social media puts you ahead of everyone else, because that's where the attention is.
sentences.zh: 我知道的是，从社交媒体起步会让你领先所有人，因为注意力就在那里。

sentences.en: Of course, there are other ways to get attention, like paid ads or starting a local business in a good location.
sentences.zh: 当然，获取注意力还有其他方式，比如付费广告，或者在好地段开一家实体店。

sentences.en: But for the person who doesn't have any money, doesn't have any starting point.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些没钱、没有任何起点的人——

sentences.en: They just have a thirst for learning and they are ambitious.
sentences.zh: 他们只有强烈的学习渴望和野心——

sentences.en: Then social media is where the attention is for the masses.
sentences.zh: 那么社交媒体就是大众注意力所在的地方。

sentences.en: That's where everyone is.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在那里。

sentences.en: And a personal brand is just the highest leverage vessel to be a creator right now.
sentences.zh: 而个人品牌，就是当下成为创作者的最高杠杆载体。

sentences.en: And it's unfortunate that it's turned into a marketable content creator identity, but that's the world we live in.
sentences.zh: 很不幸，它已经变成了一个可营销的"内容创作者"身份标签，但这就是我们生活的世界。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean you have to conform to what you think a content creator should be.
sentences.zh: 这不意味着你必须去迎合你心目中"内容创作者"该有的样子。

sentences.en: And of course, we're going to break down the one human business in a future video.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们会在之后的视频里拆解一人企业模式。

sentences.en: But the next creator bootcamp starts on September 9th.
sentences.zh: 但下一期创作者训练营 9 月 9 号就开始了。

sentences.en: So if you want to learn how to create your personal monopoly or your irreplaceable branding and create unique, heavy hitting content from your interests and learn non gimmick social media growth strategies, then consider enrolling with the link in the description.
sentences.zh: 如果你想学会如何打造你的个人垄断或者说不可替代的品牌，从你的兴趣出发创作独特、杀伤力强的内容，并学到不搞花招的社交媒体增长策略，可以考虑通过简介里的链接报名。

sentences.en: So we have our craft.
sentences.zh: 好，我们有手艺了。

sentences.en: We know how to learn.
sentences.zh: 我们知道怎么学习了。

sentences.en: We understand that we need a business.
sentences.zh: 我们明白需要一个生意了。

sentences.en: But how does AI come into play?
sentences.zh: 但 AI 是怎么参与进来的？

sentences.en: How do we achieve the impossible with AI?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么用 AI 实现不可能的事？

sentences.en: Because most people do not realize that AI is more than a slop generator and a new age search engine, they do not realize that they can quite literally ask it to build a software, a landing page, a funnel, an app, a tool, or whatever else they need to do anything on the internet.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数人没有意识到，AI 远不止是一个垃圾内容生成器和一个新时代的搜索引擎，他们没有意识到，他们完全可以叫 AI 去写一个软件、一个落地页、一个销售漏斗、一个应用、一个工具，或者任何他们在互联网上做任何事需要的东西。

sentences.en: I'm serious.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。

sentences.en: Have you tried it?
sentences.zh: 你试过吗？

sentences.en: Like, you don't need to go and build a software right now, but I would just play around with it.
sentences.zh: 你不需要现在就去做一个软件，但我建议你先玩玩看。

sentences.en: Go into Claude, go into Claude code.
sentences.zh: 打开 Claude，打开 Claude code。

sentences.en: I know that Claude code makes it sound scary, but it's just a chat box.
sentences.zh: 我知道 Claude code 这个名字听起来很吓人，但它就是个聊天框。

sentences.en: Open up clod. Click on the code tab.
sentences.zh: 打开 Claude，点那个 code 标签。

sentences.en: Think of a software that you want to build a to do app and then just say, Hey Claude, how can I go about building a to do app with you?
sentences.zh: 想一个你想做的软件，比如一个待办事项 app，然后直接说：嘿 Claude，我该怎么跟你一起做一个待办事项 app？

sentences.en: And then it'll tell you.
sentences.zh: 然后它就会告诉你。

sentences.en: And if you want to actually learn along the way, you just ask it, okay, what's the best way to do this?
sentences.zh: 如果你想在这个过程中真正学到东西，你就问它：好，做这件事的最佳方式是什么？

sentences.en: And then you make the decisions along the way.
sentences.zh: 然后你在过程中自己做决定。

sentences.en: And if it does something that you don't know how to do, you ask it to teach you what it did.
sentences.zh: 如果它做了什么你不懂的操作，你就让它教你它刚才做了什么。

sentences.en: Now, if you do this for one, two, three days, you will have a crazy app and you'll be like, oh my gosh, I get it now.
sentences.zh: 你只要这样做个一、二、三天，你就会做出一个很疯狂的 app，然后你会说：天哪，我现在懂了。

sentences.en: And the objection there is.
sentences.zh: 这时候会有人反驳。

sentences.en: But Dan, that just leads to AI slop.
sentences.zh: 但 Dan，那只会产生一堆 AI 垃圾。

sentences.en: Correct? Because that's where most people stop.
sentences.zh: 说得没错，因为大多数人就停在那里了。

sentences.en: They don't realize that iteration exists and that your first iteration would suck with or without AI.
sentences.zh: 他们没有意识到迭代的存在，也不知道你的第一版无论有没有 AI 都会很烂。

sentences.en: We went over this in another video, but there are more mobile apps than ever.
sentences.zh: 我们在另一个视频里讲过，现在的手机 app 比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: But the usage of mobile apps has stayed around the same.
sentences.zh: 但手机 app 的使用量基本没变。

sentences.en: Or the CEO, I think.
sentences.zh: 还是那个 CEO，我想。

sentences.en: I think it was the CEO of the company that's creating GTA six.
sentences.zh: 我想是那个在做 GTA 6 的公司的 CEO。

sentences.en: He had a quote in a podcast where he's like, you could create a video game ten years ago whenever you wanted.
sentences.zh: 他在一个播客里说过一句话，大意是：十年前你随时都可以去做一个电子游戏。

sentences.en: You could have learned it and built it, but you didn't. And even if you did, it probably wasn't going to be a hit.
sentences.zh: 你本可以去学、去把它做出来，但你没有。就算你做了，它大概率也不会火。

sentences.en: It wasn't going to be something that people cared about.
sentences.zh: 它不会成为人们真正在意的东西。

sentences.en: And then he went on to say that we create hits because obviously GTA six is a hit.
sentences.zh: 然后他接着说，我们能做出爆款，是因为 GTA 6 显然就是一个爆款。

sentences.en: And even if you created something close to GTA six, that doesn't mean that it would get distribution.
sentences.zh: 但就算你做出一款接近 GTA 6 的东西，也不意味着你能获得分发。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that you'd actually get it in front of other people's hands and make millions upon millions of dollars, or actually understand how to manage that size of a company, or organize that size of a project with AI or without it.
sentences.zh: 不意味着你真的能把它送到别人手里，赚到几百万几千万美元，也不意味着你真的懂怎么管理那种规模的公司，或者用 AI 或不用 AI 去组织那种规模的项目。

sentences.en: There is so much more to the equation.
sentences.zh: 这个等式里还有太多其他东西。

sentences.en: AI is just one massive form of leverage.
sentences.zh: AI 只是一种巨大的杠杆形式。

sentences.en: You still have to go and learn and do all of the other things associated with building a business or your life's work.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要去学习、去做所有其他跟构建一个生意或你毕生事业相关的事情。

sentences.en: People just don't like to see that.
sentences.zh: 人们就是不愿意看到这一点。

sentences.en: They just think, oh, AI just creates a bunch of slop and it does just create a bunch of slop, but that doesn't mean that it's useless.
sentences.zh: 他们只会想，哦，AI 就是产出一堆垃圾，它确实产出了一堆垃圾，但这不代表它没用。

sentences.en: This is black and white thinking.
sentences.zh: 这是非黑即白的思维。

sentences.en: Stop thinking you're so intelligent when you're obviously making a very stupid mistake with your thinking.
sentences.zh: 别再觉得自己多聪明了，你这种思维方式显然在犯一个非常愚蠢的错误。

sentences.en: So the landing page that you build starts as a rough draft.
sentences.zh: 所以你做的那个落地页，一开始就是一个草稿。

sentences.en: Then it's up to you to make micro adjustments until it's actually effective.
sentences.zh: 然后由你来做微调，直到它真正有效。

sentences.en: The software you build will be extremely buggy and look horrible until you fix the bugs over and over again, until it's better than 99% of apps on the market.
sentences.zh: 你做的软件一开始会 bug 满天飞、丑得要命，直到你一遍又一遍地修 bug，修到它比市面上 99% 的应用都好。

sentences.en: Most people just don't have that level of persistence and iteration.
sentences.zh: 大多数人就是没有那种程度的坚持和迭代能力。

sentences.en: In short, people just aren't high agency.
sentences.zh: 说白了，大多数人就是不够高能动性。

sentences.en: People don't understand that.
sentences.zh: 人们不明白这一点。

sentences.en: They can just ask, how can I do this and continue asking questions until a clear plan is formed?
sentences.zh: 他们完全可以去问"我该怎么做"，然后不断追问，直到一个清晰的计划成型。

sentences.en: Then have the AI execute on your vision that you choose and control not a random guess, and proceed to iterate until it is valuable.
sentences.zh: 然后让 AI 去执行你选择和掌控的愿景，而不是随机瞎猜，接着持续迭代，直到它有价值。

sentences.en: That's the other thing people don't seem to understand is that the AI slop was chosen to be put out by someone.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎不明白的另一件事是：那些 AI 垃圾是有人选择把它发出来的。

sentences.en: That just demonstrates the level of development of the people who are putting out the AI slop.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰说明了那些产出 AI 垃圾的人处于什么水平。

sentences.en: So I want to give you a quick start guide to do anything with AI.
sentences.zh: 所以我想给你一个用 AI 做任何事的快速入门指南。

sentences.en: First is you need to know what you want, and you need to know what good looks like.
sentences.zh: 第一，你得知道自己想要什么，还得知道"好"是什么样。

sentences.en: Because for most of you, you're going to use AI to build a one person business.
sentences.zh: 因为对你们大多数人来说，你会用 AI 去建一个一人企业。

sentences.en: And if you don't know how to build a business, then you're going to expect the AI to do it perfectly for you without knowing what you need.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道怎么做生意，你就会指望 AI 在你不知道自己需要什么的情况下，完美地帮你搞定一切。

sentences.en: It still takes years of iteration to see any form of success.
sentences.zh: 看到任何形式的成功，仍然需要多年的迭代。

sentences.en: Nothing has changed in that regard.
sentences.zh: 这一点没有任何改变。

sentences.en: You still need marketing. You still need product.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要营销。你仍然需要产品。

sentences.en: You still need sales.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要销售。

sentences.en: You still need distribution.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要分发渠道。

sentences.en: You still need all of the things you needed in the past.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要过去所需的一切。

sentences.en: But if you know what you want, what you need, and what good looks like, then you can simply ask the AI how it can help you accomplish those goals and go from there.
sentences.zh: 但如果你知道自己想要什么、需要什么、以及"好"是什么样，那你就可以直接问 AI 它能怎么帮你达成这些目标，然后从那里开始。

sentences.en: The best place to start is by simply using AI as a tailored learning tool.
sentences.zh: 最好的起点就是把 AI 当作一个为你量身定制的学习工具。

sentences.en: Use it to learn, offer creation or copywriting or social media.
sentences.zh: 用它来学 offer 设计、文案写作或者社交媒体。

sentences.en: You can't have AI do something for you if you don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 如果你自己都不知道要做什么，你就没法让 AI 替你做。

sentences.en: Number two is to have absurdly high standards, because the reason every response you get from AI is slop is that you treat the first draft as the final draft.
sentences.zh: 第二，要有高得离谱的标准，因为你从 AI 那里得到的每一个回答之所以是垃圾，是因为你把初稿当成了终稿。

sentences.en: You don't understand that you will still have to tweak every little design feature, word, sentence, or whatever else you are having.
sentences.zh: 你不明白你仍然需要去调整每一个设计细节、每一个词、每一句话，或者你正在做的任何东西。

sentences.en: The AI do what you create with AI sucks because you see AI as this thing that should just be an absolute genius, rather than seeing it as a tool that meets your level of intelligence and ambition.
sentences.zh: 你用 AI 做出来的东西很烂，是因为你把 AI 看成是一个绝对天才，而不是一个能匹配你智力和野心的工具。

sentences.en: Number three is to try to replace yourself with AI.
sentences.zh: 第三，试着用 AI 替代你自己。

sentences.en: Yes, I believe the best way to learn AI is to try to automate yourself out of work.
sentences.zh: 是的，我相信学 AI 最好的方式就是试着把自己从工作中自动化出去。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because you will quickly learn what can and can't be automated yet.
sentences.zh: 因为你很快就能搞清楚什么能自动化、什么还不能。

sentences.en: And if you try to continue to automate the things that can't be automated, then you're just going to fall behind and it's not going to work.
sentences.zh: 如果你硬要去自动化那些还不能自动化的东西，那你只会落后，而且行不通。

sentences.en: And so once you understand what can and can't be automated, then only you can choose which parts of your business and craft to delegate to AI.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你理解了什么能自动化、什么不能，只有你才能选择把生意和手艺的哪些部分交给 AI。

sentences.en: For me, AI is obviously great at building landing pages and funnels and going through large swaths of information so I can research and find patterns and trends.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，AI 显然很擅长做落地页、漏斗，以及处理海量信息，让我能去做研究、发现模式和趋势。

sentences.en: And since I know what good looks like because I've built landing pages, I've built the funnels and I know what leads to results, then I know how to guide the AI to get to that point, because the first draft obviously isn't going to get there.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道"好"是什么样——我做过落地页，我做过漏斗，我知道什么能带来结果——所以我知道怎么引导 AI 达到那个点，因为初稿显然到不了那里。

sentences.en: And for content strategy, it would be silly of me at this point to manually research YouTube videos and tweets and other things that are viral or trends or things that are working, because that now puts you at a massive disadvantage.
sentences.zh: 至于内容策略，如果我现在还手动去研究哪些 YouTube 视频、推文在爆、哪些是趋势、哪些有效，那就太蠢了，因为这会让你处于巨大的劣势。

sentences.en: That's strategy.
sentences.zh: 那才是策略。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You have to understand, you have to study and gather the Intel and information to create a winning strategy based on what has won in the past and what is winning now.
sentences.zh: 你必须理解，必须去研究、收集情报和信息，基于过去赢过的东西和现在正在赢的东西，制定一个能赢的策略。

sentences.en: You obviously don't want to play a losing hand because you haven't studied what's winning.
sentences.zh: 你显然不想打一手必输的牌，就因为你没研究过什么在赢。

sentences.en: So that's why you now use AI to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么你现在要用 AI 来做这件事。

sentences.en: And that's part of why we built Eden, because I feel like that's one of the most effective ways to use AI.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们构建 Eden 的部分原因，因为我觉得这是使用 AI 最高效的方式之一。

sentences.en: So if you're a creator or a writer or someone who researches and writes and wants a creative workspace, then consider trying Eden Link in the description.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一个创作者、写作者，或者做研究和写作、想要一个创造性工作空间的人，可以考虑试试描述里的 Eden 链接。

sentences.en: And there's videos on the Eden Channel.
sentences.zh: Eden 频道上也有相关视频。

sentences.en: There's a full eating guide, there's my entire content strategy, and there's an Instagram growth guide.
sentences.zh: 有一份完整的 Eden 指南，有我的整套内容策略，还有一份 Instagram 增长指南。

sentences.en: And I'm just going to be going through the platforms.
sentences.zh: 而且我会逐个平台讲过去。

sentences.en: So how to grow on different platforms and how to write or create each specific type of posts.
sentences.zh: 也就是如何在不同平台上增长，以及如何写或创作每种特定类型的内容。

sentences.en: So Substack newsletters or X articles or tweets or Instagram carousels or things like that.
sentences.zh: 比如 Substack 邮件、X 文章、推文、Instagram 轮播图之类的东西。

sentences.en: So the Eden Channel itself is just going to be a repository that you can go to when you want to learn how to master social media, and that's the research side of things.
sentences.zh: 所以 Eden 频道本身就是一个资源库，当你想学怎么玩转社交媒体的时候就可以去那里看，这是研究的那一面。

sentences.en: But when it comes to actually writing the newsletter, the post, the script itself one, I like the creative process of writing, so I make it a part of my day.
sentences.zh: 但到了真正写邮件、写帖子、写脚本的时候，第一，我喜欢写作的创作过程，所以我把它变成我一天的一部分。

sentences.en: Two the value of writing is in the eyes of the reader.
sentences.zh: 第二，写作的价值在于读者的眼睛。

sentences.en: With code.
sentences.zh: 代码也一样。

sentences.en: No end user cares about what the code looks like.
sentences.zh: 没有哪个终端用户在乎代码长什么样。

sentences.en: They don't see it.
sentences.zh: 他们根本看不到。

sentences.en: They care about if it's beneficial to them.
sentences.zh: 他们在乎的是这东西对他们有没有用。

sentences.en: That's why I write, because it gives me fine tuned control over the value provided.
sentences.zh: 这就是我写作的原因，因为它让我能精细地控制我提供的价值。

sentences.en: So if you don't know where to start with automating yourself or trying to use AI to replace you, just think of anything that you do on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不知道从哪里开始自动化自己，或者尝试用 AI 替代你，就想一想你每天做的任何事。

sentences.en: Literally write down what you do at every time throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 把你一天中每个时间点做的事都写下来，真的写下来。

sentences.en: Then give that list to AI and ask what could be turned into a repeatable process with a prompt, a skill, a tool, a software, or whatever, and it will give you some options.
sentences.zh: 然后把那个清单交给 AI，问它哪些可以变成一个可重复的流程，用一段提示词、一个技能、一个工具、一个软件或随便什么，它会给你一些选项。

sentences.en: And of course, understand that that automation, that prompt, that skill, that tool, software that you build is also a first draft.
sentences.zh: 当然，要明白那个自动化、那段提示词、那个技能、那个工具、你构建的软件，也是一个初稿。

sentences.en: And it will suck at first and you'll see it and you'll be like, well, this isn't helpful at all, but that's because you're not treating AI as a digital employee.
sentences.zh: 它一开始会很烂，你看到它的时候会觉得，这根本没什么用，但那是因为你没有把 AI 当成一个数字员工。

sentences.en: You don't understand management or training.
sentences.zh: 你不懂管理，也不懂培训。

sentences.en: When you bring on an employee, they don't just automatically know how to do every single thing inside of the business.
sentences.zh: 当你招一个员工进来，他们不会自动就知道公司里的每一件事该怎么做。

sentences.en: You have to train them.
sentences.zh: 你必须培训他们。

sentences.en: You have to teach them exactly how you want it done, step by step in one little prompt.
sentences.zh: 你必须一步一步地教他们你希望怎么做，就在一段小小的提示词里。

sentences.en: Or the AI guessing obviously isn't going to get there.
sentences.zh: 不然让 AI 自己猜，显然不可能达到那个水平。

sentences.en: So you have to communicate back and forth until it gets to that point, and then boom, you have the repeatable process.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须来回沟通，直到它达到那个点，然后砰的一声，你就有了一个可重复的流程。

sentences.en: Now, in future videos, we're going to dive into everything that we've mentioned in this video the digital renaissance, how to learn effectively, the best skills to learn how to use AI, how to think with clarity and more.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的视频里，我们会深入讲这个视频里提到的一切：数字文艺复兴、如何高效学习、最值得学的技能、怎么用 AI、怎么清晰思考，还有更多。

sentences.en: So thank you for watching this video.
sentences.zh: 感谢观看这个视频。

sentences.en: I hope it opened your mind. Subscribe.
sentences.zh: 希望这期视频打开了你的思路。订阅。

sentences.en: Like check the links in the description.
sentences.zh: 点赞，看看简介里的链接。

sentences.en: I'll see you in the next one. Bye.
sentences.zh: 下期见。拜。
